words.definition: the theory that living organisms are composed of cells, cells are the basic units of life and cells arise from pre-existing cells
words.example: Cell theory provides a unifying explanation for the organization of living organisms.

words.definition: an instrument that produces an enlarged image of objects too small to see clearly with the unaided eye
words.example: A microscope allows biologists to examine cells and tissues.

words.definition: a microscope that uses visible light and glass lenses to form an image
words.example: A light microscope can be used to observe living cells.

words.definition: a microscope that uses a beam of electrons to produce images with very high resolution
words.example: An electron microscope reveals cell ultrastructure in much greater detail than a light microscope.

words.definition: the ratio of image size to actual size
words.example: Magnification can be calculated by dividing image size by actual size.

words.definition: the ability to distinguish two nearby points as separate
words.example: Electron microscopes have higher resolution than light microscopes.

words.definition: an image of a specimen produced using a microscope
words.example: The micrograph shows mitochondria within a cell.

words.definition: a cell lacking a nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles
words.example: Bacteria are made of prokaryotic cells.

words.definition: a cell containing a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles
words.example: Animal and plant cells are eukaryotic.

words.definition: a rigid layer outside the plasma membrane that supports and protects certain cells
words.example: Plant cell walls contain cellulose.

words.definition: the selectively permeable membrane that surrounds the cytoplasm of a cell
words.example: The plasma membrane controls movement of substances into and out of the cell.

words.definition: the internal cell material outside the nucleus, including cytosol and suspended structures
words.example: Many metabolic reactions occur in the cytoplasm.

words.definition: a cellular structure that carries out protein synthesis by translating mRNA
words.example: Ribosomes join amino acids into polypeptides.

words.definition: a membrane-bound organelle in eukaryotic cells that contains most of the cell's DNA
words.example: The nucleus stores chromosomes in a eukaryotic cell.

words.definition: a double-membrane organelle where most aerobic ATP production occurs in eukaryotic cells
words.example: Mitochondria are abundant in cells with high energy demands.

words.definition: a membrane network studded with ribosomes that synthesizes and processes proteins for secretion or membranes
words.example: Secretory cells often contain extensive rough endoplasmic reticulum.

words.definition: a stack of membrane sacs that modifies, sorts and packages proteins and lipids
words.example: The Golgi apparatus packages proteins into vesicles.

words.definition: a small membrane-bound sac used for transport or storage within cells
words.example: Transport vesicles move proteins from the ER to the Golgi apparatus.

words.definition: a membrane-bound compartment used mainly for storage and water balance
words.example: A large central vacuole helps maintain turgor in plant cells.

words.definition: a membrane-bound organelle containing hydrolytic enzymes for intracellular digestion
words.example: Lysosomes break down damaged cell components and engulfed material.

words.definition: a network of protein filaments that supports cell shape, organization and movement
words.example: The cytoskeleton helps position organelles and move materials inside cells.

words.definition: a cylindrical structure made of microtubules that helps organize the spindle in many animal cells
words.example: Centrioles contribute to spindle organization during animal-cell division.
